_comment: Display fixtures for the object inventory. hassemu creates one `device` plus five
states per display, so what varies between displays is not a device TYPE but the
SHAPE of what the adapter knows about them — which is what the object texts, the
auto-naming and the stored tokens depend on. Each display reaches the adapter from its
own address (X-Forwarded-For with trustProxy on — the only way to give a loopback
harness several source addresses); `ptr` is its reverse-DNS answer, served by
test/inventory-dns-hook.cjs. The adapter mints a random id per display; the inventory
maps those to stable `display-N` keys, so two runs stay byte-identical.
Not here on purpose: authRequired — it changes no object (only the auth guard), and a
second controller run for it would add nothing the unit tests do not cover.
Every address is from 192.0.2.0/24 (RFC 5737, never routed): the adapter probes the
dashboard host, and a real private address could reach a real device on the machine

displays.comment: Auto-named after its IP — a display whose reverse DNS yields nothing (the LAN norm for a DHCP client without a PTR record).

No choice made — the display sits on the landing page. Its name is adapter-assigned like every other, because a name the USER typed in the admin is not adapter output and has no place in an inventory of what the adapter creates (the guarantee that such a name survives is unit-tested instead).
A discovered dashboard picked directly from the dropdown (the third step of the resolver chain).
A Companion app that went through the sign-in — its tokens are stored on the device object.
